title: The rich man and Lazaros — the hollow places of the dead in 1 Enoch and 2 Esdras
summary_md: The parable assumes a place the pulpit has never been able to describe. Lazaros dies and *was carried by the angels into Abraham’s bosom: the rich man also died, and was buried;* (Luke 16:22). The rich man is awake there: *And in hell he lift up his eyes, being in torments, and sees Abraham afar off, and Lazarus in his bosom.* (Luke 16:23). And the two places do not touch: *And beside all this, between us and you there is a great gulf fixed: so that they which would pass from hence to you cannot; neither can they pass to us, that would come from thence.* (Luke 16:26). Enoch was shown that very place. *And there was in it four hollow places, deep and wide and very smooth. How smooth are the hollow places and deep and dark to look at.* (1 Enoch 22:2). The angel told him what they are for: *Then Raphael answered, one of the holy angels who was with me, and said unto me: ‘These hollow places have been created for this very purpose, that the spirits of the souls of the dead should assemble therein, yea that all the souls of the children of men should assemble here.* (1 Enoch 22:3), and how long they are for: *And these places have been made to receive them till the day of their judgement and till their appointed period [till the period appointed], till the great judgement (comes) upon them.’* (1 Enoch 22:4). The dead are awake, they are kept apart, and the keeping has an end. The righteous have their own division with the bright spring of water, and the sinners theirs, set apart in pain till the great day (1 Enoch 22:9-11). That is why the parable can speak of torment and of comfort in the same hour without either being the last word. The last word is the resurrection out of those places: *And the earth shall restore those that are asleep in her, and so shall the dust those that dwell in silence, and the secret places shall deliver those souls that were committed to them.* (2 Esdras 7:32). When Abraham says they would not be persuaded though one rose from the dead, he is speaking of a rising out of exactly these chambers.

title: As it was in the days of Noach — the flood judgment in 1 Enoch and Jubilees
summary_md: When Yahusha (Jesus) wants to tell his disciples what his own day will look like, he reaches for the flood. *And as it was in the days of Noe, so shall it be also in the days of the Son of Adam.* (Luke 17:26). *They did eat, they drank, they married wives, they were given in marriage, until the day that Noe entered into the ark, and the flood came, and destroyed them all.* (Luke 17:27). The flood he points to is the one Enoch describes, and Enoch gives it a cause and a purpose that Genesis compresses. The warning went to Noah by the hand of an angel: *’Go to Noah and tell him in my name “Hide thyself!” and reveal to him the end that is approaching: that the whole earth will be destroyed, and a deluge is about to come upon the whole earth, and will destroy all that is on it.* (1 Enoch 10:2). The purpose was a seed carried through: *And now instruct him that he may escape and his seed may be preserved for all the generations of the world.’* (1 Enoch 10:3). Jubilees names what had filled the earth by then: *lawlessness increased on the earth and all flesh corrupted its way* (Jubilees 5:2), and the decree that answered it: *I shall destroy man and all flesh upon the face of the earth which I have created* (Jubilees 5:4). So the eating and drinking and marrying of Luke 17:27 are not innocence; they are a world going about its business on the eve of a judgment it had been warned of, while one household was told to hide itself and was kept. The days of the Son of Adam run the same way, a corrupted order judged and a seed preserved through it, and the ones who are busy with the ordinary things are the ones the day overtakes.

title: The Son of Adam is come to seek and save the lost — the gathering of the tribes of Jacob in Sirach and 1 Enoch
summary_md: At the house of Zakkay (Zacchaeus) the King says what he came for: *For the Son of Adam is come to seek and to save that which was lost.* (Luke 19:10). The lost he means are a people, the house of Yashar'el (Israel) scattered and gone from memory, and the library had been praying for their return long before he said it. Sirach asks for it by name: *gather all the tribes of Jacob together, and inherit you them, as from the beginning* (Sirach (Ecclesiasticus) 36:11), all the tribes and not Yahudah (Judah) alone, and names the people he is asking for: *have mercy upon the people that is called by your name, and upon Yashar'el (Israel), whom you have named your firstborn* (Sirach 36:12). Enoch saw the same gathering in his vision of the sheep. When the great horn was raised among the flock, *And it looked at them [and their eyes opened], and it cried to the sheep, and the rams saw it and all ran to it.* (1 Enoch 90:10). And at the end of the vision the whole scattered flock comes home: *And all that had been destroyed and dispersed, and all the beasts of the field, and all the birds of the heaven, assembled in that house, and Yahuah (Lord) of the sheep rejoiced with great joy because they were all good and had returned to His house.* (1 Enoch 90:33). Seeking and saving the lost is shepherd's work, and the sheep he is seeking are the ones that were devoured and scattered through the long periods of the shepherds. Sirach prayed it, Enoch saw it, and at Zakkay's table the Son of Adam says he has come to do it.

title: The multitude of the heavenly host — the innumerable host praising before Yahuah of Spirits in 1 Enoch
summary_md: Over the shepherds' fields the sky fills: *And suddenly there was with the angel a multitude of the heavenly host praising Elohim (God), and saying,* (Luke 2:13) *Glory to Elohim (God) in the highest, and on earth peace, good will toward men.* (Luke 2:14). Enoch had already stood in front of that host. *And after that I saw thousands of thousands and ten thousand times ten thousand, I saw a multitude beyond number and reckoning, who stood before Yahuah (Lord) of Spirits.* (1 Enoch 40:1). He heard what they do there, day and night: *Those who sleep not bless Thee: they stand before Thy glory and bless, praise, and extol, saying: “Holy, holy, holy, is Yahuah (Lord) of Spirits: He filleth the earth with spirits.”’* (1 Enoch 39:12), and again, *And here my eyes saw all those who sleep not: they stand before Him and bless and say: ‘Blessed be Thou, and blessed be the name of Yahuah (Lord) for ever and ever.’* (1 Enoch 39:13). The host that never sleeps and never stops blessing before the throne is the host that came down over Bethlehem the night the Word was born in flesh. Their song did not change when they came down; the glory they give in the highest is the same blessing Enoch heard them give, now sounded over a stable because the One they bless had come to the earth.
note: The two Enoch 'citations' were really quotes in the old wording (40:1, 39:12-13 differ in the live text); re-quoted from the live verses, Luke kept.

title: Equal unto the angels — the children of the resurrection dwelling with the angels in 1 Enoch
summary_md: The Sadducees deny the resurrection and Yahusha (Jesus) answers them with what the raised will be: *They which shall be accounted worthy to obtain that world, and the resurrection from the dead, neither marry, nor are given in marriage* (Luke 20:35), *Neither can they die any more: for they are equal unto the angels; and are the children of Elohim (God), being the children of the resurrection.* (Luke 20:36). Enoch was carried to the place where that life is already laid up. *And there I saw another vision, the dwelling-places of the holy, And the resting-places of the righteous.* (1 Enoch 39:4). *Here mine eyes saw their dwellings with His righteous angels, And their resting-places with the holy. And they petitioned and interceded and prayed for the children of men, And righteousness flowed before them as water, And mercy like dew upon the earth: Thus it is amongst them for ever and ever.* (1 Enoch 39:5). And at the end of the book the righteous are told plainly what they are being kept for: *Be hopeful; for aforetime ye were put to shame through ill and affliction; but now ye shall shine as the lights of heaven, ye shall shine and ye shall be seen, and the portals of heaven shall be opened to you.* (1 Enoch 104:2). *Be hopeful, and cast not away your hope; for ye shall have great joy as the angels of heaven.* (1 Enoch 104:4). *And now fear not, ye righteous, when ye see the sinners growing strong and prospering in their ways: be not companions with them, but keep afar from their violence; for ye shall become companions of the hosts of heaven.* (1 Enoch 104:6). Equal unto the angels, companions of the hosts of heaven, dwelling with the righteous angels: it is one picture. Daniel saw the same people rise to it: *And many of them that sleep in the dust of the earth shall awake, some to everlasting life, and some to shame and everlasting contempt.* (Daniel 12:2). *And they that be wise shall shine as the brightness of the firmament; and they that turn many to righteousness as the stars for ever and ever.* (Daniel 12:3). The King grounds it in the bush, where the Elohim (God) of Abraham, of Isaac, and of Jacob is not the Elohim (God) of the dead but of the living; the fathers are not gone, they are kept, and the resting-places Enoch saw are where they wait to shine.
note: The old Enoch 'citations' were quotes in old wording (39:4-5 reworded; the old 104:4 words are not at 104:4); re-quoted 39:4-5 and 104:2, 104:4, 104:6 from the live text; Daniel added from the index; Exodus 3:6 named in prose.

title: Hereafter shall the Son of Adam sit on the right hand of the power of Elohim (Psalm 110; Daniel 7)
summary_md:
Before the council they ask, *Art thou the Messiah (Christ)? tell us* (Luke 22:67), and Yahusha (Jesus) answers with a throne: *Hereafter shall the Son of Adam sit on the right hand of the power of Elohim (God).* (Luke 22:69). He names himself by David's oracle and by Daniel's vision at once.

David heard the Father speak it: *Yahuah (LORD) said unto my Lord, Sit thou at my right hand, until I make thine enemies thy footstool* (Psalm 110:1); the Father seats the Son at his own right hand. And Daniel saw it given in heaven: *I saw in the night visions, and, behold, one like the Son of Adam came with the clouds of heaven, and came to the Ancient of days, and they brought him near before him.* (Daniel 7:13). The likeness is kept in the words, one *like* the Son of Adam, because the Formed Son came in flesh and was brought near before the Father, and the dominion was handed to him there: *And there was given him dominion, and glory, and a kingdom, that all people, nations, and languages, should serve him: his dominion is an everlasting dominion, which shall not pass away, and his kingdom that which shall not be destroyed.* (Daniel 7:14). It is given him. The Son is enthroned by the Father; he never seizes what is the Father's to bestow.

Peter, once converted and strengthening his brethren, preaches this very throne: *For David is not ascended into the heavens: but he says himself, Yahuah (LORD) said unto my Lord, Sit you on my right hand,* (Acts 2:34). And Enoch saw the same seating and the same faces looking on it. *And Yahuah (Lord) of Spirits seated him on the throne of His glory, And the spirit of righteousness was poured out upon him, And the word of his mouth slays all the sinners, And all the unrighteous are destroyed from before his face.* (1 Enoch 62:2). *And one portion of them shall look on the other, And they shall be terrified, And they shall be downcast of countenance, And pain shall seize them, When they see that Son of Adam Sitting on the throne of his glory.* (1 Enoch 62:5). The men who blindfolded him and struck him are told to their faces where they will next see him, and Enoch had already written down what their faces will do when they do.

title: Paradise and the chambers of the souls of the dead in 1 Enoch
summary_md: To the thief beside him the King says a word about where they are both going before the day is out: *And Yahusha (Jesus) said unto him, Verily I say unto you, To day shall you be with me in paradise.* (Luke 23:43). Enoch had been shown the place. *And there was in it four hollow places, deep and wide and very smooth. How smooth are the hollow places and deep and dark to look at.* (1 Enoch 22:2). *And these places have been made to receive them till the day of their judgement and till their appointed period [till the period appointed], till the great judgement (comes) upon them.’* (1 Enoch 22:4). The dead are not all kept in one room: *And he answered me and said unto me: ‘These three have been made that the spirits of the dead might be separated. And such a division has been made for the spirits of the righteous, in which there is the bright spring of water.* (1 Enoch 22:9). The paradise the thief was promised that same day is the righteous division of those chambers, the one with the bright spring, set apart from the chamber of the sinners who wait in pain for the great day. The King went there that day, and the thief with him. The rich man and Lazaros in Luke 16 look across the gulf between those same divisions, and when Paul says he ascended on high and led captivity captive, the captives he led out are the ones who had been waiting by that spring. The chambers Enoch walked through are what Luke names with a single word.

title: The genealogy back to Adam, the son of Elohim — the seed of Adam in Jubilees and 1 Enoch
summary_md: Luke runs his genealogy backward until it can go no further: *Which was the son of Enos, which was the son of Seth, which was the son of Adam, which was the son of Elohim (God).* (Luke 3:38). That line, father to son back to the man Elohim (God) formed, is the thread the whole promise hangs on, and the library watched it being kept. Jubilees tells how it was carried past the first murder: *And Adam and his wife mourned for Abel four weeks of years, and in the fourth year of the fifth week they became joyful, and Adam knew his wife again, and she bare him a son, and he called his name Seth; for he said “Elohim (God) has raised up a second seed to us on the earth instead of Abel; for Cain slew him.”* (Jubilees 4:7). Enoch saw the same line in his first dream, as cattle. *Before I took thy mother Edna, I saw in a vision on my bed, and behold a bull came forth from the earth, and that bull was white; and after it came forth a heifer, and along with this (latter) came forth two bulls, one of them black and the other red.* (1 Enoch 85:3). The black bull gores the red one, and then the second seed comes: *And after that she bore another white bull, and after him she bore many bulls and black cows.* (1 Enoch 85:8). *And I saw in my sleep that white bull likewise grow and become a great white bull, and from him proceeded many white bulls, and they resembled him.* (1 Enoch 85:9). White bull following white bull, each resembling the one before, is Seth's line going down the generations, and Luke's list is that same line read upward. Enoch counts himself in it from the same head: Adam is *the seventh from Adam, the first man whom Yahuah (Lord) of Spirits created* (1 Enoch 60:8), and Jude counts the same way: *And Enoch also, the seventh from Adam, prophesied of these, saying, Behold, Yahuah (Lord) comes with ten thousands of his saints,* (Jude 1:14). Luke, Jubilees, Enoch, and Jude are all counting the same fathers, and the count ends where Luke ends it, at the son of Elohim (God).

title: Legion into the deep — the spirits of the giants and the place of condemnation in 1 Enoch and Jubilees
summary_md: The spirits in the man at Gerasa know who has come ashore: *When he saw Yahusha (Jesus), he cried out, and fell down before him, and with a loud voice said, What have I to do with you, Yahusha (Jesus), you Son of Elohim (God) most high? I beseech you, torment me not.* (Luke 8:28). And they know where they are headed: *And they besought him that he would not command them to go out into the deep.* (Luke 8:31). Enoch tells where such spirits came from and why they dread the deep. *And now, the giants, who are produced from the spirits and flesh, shall be called evil spirits upon the earth, and on the earth shall be their dwelling.* (1 Enoch 15:8). *Evil spirits have proceeded from their bodies; because they are born from men and from the holy Watchers is their beginning and primal origin; they shall be evil spirits on earth, and evil spirits shall they be called.* (1 Enoch 15:9). They have a season, and it has an end already written: *From the days of the slaughter and destruction and death of the giants, from the souls of whose flesh the spirits, having gone forth, shall destroy without incurring judgement—thus shall they destroy until the day of the consummation, the great judgement in which the age shall be consummated, over the Watchers and the godless, yea, shall be wholly consummated.”* (1 Enoch 16:1). Noah asked for them to be shut away before the end: *And You know how Your Watchers, the fathers of these spirits, acted in my day: and as for these spirits which are living, imprison them and hold them fast in the place of condemnation, and let them not bring destruction on the sons of your servant, my Elohim (God); for these are malignant, and created in order to destroy.* (Jubilees 10:5). So Legion is begging not to be sent early to the place Noah prayed them into and Enoch said they are bound for. The torment they fear is the deep before their appointed day, and the One standing on the shore in flesh is the One who holds that day.

title: The Magi and the Book of Luminaries
summary_md: *Now when Yahusha (Jesus) was born in Bethlehem of Judaea in the days of Herod the king, behold, there came wise men from the east to Jerusalem,* (Matthew 2:1) *Saying, Where is he that is born King of the Yahudim (Jews)? for we have seen his star in the east, and are come to worship him.* (Matthew 2:2). Men who read the heavens for a king were not working from nothing. The library carries a whole book on the subject, and it opens by saying where the knowledge came from: *The book of the courses of the luminaries of the heaven, the relations of each, according to their classes, their dominion and their seasons, according to their names and places of origin, and according to their months, which Uriel, the holy angel, who was with me, who is their guide, showed me; and he showed me all their laws exactly as they are, and how it is with regard to all the years of the world and unto eternity, till the new creation is accomplished which dureth till eternity.* (1 Enoch 72:1). That is the Book of Luminaries, 1 Enoch 72–82, the heavens read as law and appointed season rather than as omen. Daniel stood at the head of the wise men of Babylon and Persia, and a learning like Enoch's in the hands of men like Daniel's is where the Magi's watching came from. Enoch's second dream, the vision of the sheep in chapters 89–90, ends with a great horn raised among the flock and a white bull before whom all the beasts bow, and men who held that book knew there was one to look for. The star over Judea and the men who followed it belong inside that tradition, not outside it.
note: Mentioned Enoch without a verse; 72:1 was quoted in the old text and stands live, now cited; 'extras-tier witness' and 'Hebrew library' labels removed; Matthew quoted in full from the index.

title: Many be called, but few chosen — 1 Enoch 48 and 2 Esdras 8 on the broad call and the few
summary_md: The parable of the laborers closes on a hard line: *So the last shall be first, and the first last: for many be called, but few chosen.* (Matthew 20:16). The call goes out broadly because the sheep are scattered everywhere and no one can tell them by sight, and the chosen are the ones who were his before the call ever reached them. He says it himself in John 10: *ye believe not, because ye are not of my sheep ... my sheep hear my voice.* The hearing does not make a sheep; it shows one. Enoch saw the broad call as a fountain anyone could come to: *And in that place I saw the fountain of righteousness Which was inexhaustible: And around it were many fountains of wisdom: And all the thirsty drank of them, And were filled with wisdom, And their dwellings were with the righteous and holy and elect.* (1 Enoch 48:1). And he saw who the Son of Adam was kept for: *And the wisdom of Yahuah (Lord) of Spirits hath revealed him to the holy and righteous; For he hath preserved the lot of the righteous, Because they have hated and despised this world of unrighteousness, And have hated all its works and ways in the name of Yahuah (Lord) of Spirits: For in his name they are saved, And according to his good pleasure hath it been in regard to their life.* (1 Enoch 48:7). Ezra was told the same count in plainer arithmetic: *there be many created, but few shall be saved* (2 Esdras 8:3). The many are not cheated; the call really went out to them. The few are the ones written from the foundation of the world (Revelation 13:8), who heard because they were his, and who then walked in it, because the warning about being blotted out is spoken to the wheat and never to the tares. The last made first are the scattered ones nobody expected, and the first made last are the ones who stood in the field all day and never bore the fruit.
note: Old summary was almost entirely internal shorthand (Red Line #11, substance chains, Reformed/Arminian labels); rewritten in plain words around 48:1 and 48:7 (live); the old 39:1 quote dropped (39:1 is a Noah fragment about the descent of the holy children and does not carry the thought); John 10 and 2 Esdras 8:3 kept as the old summary quoted them; title plainer.

title: The Son of Adam enthroned on the throne of glory in the Parables of Enoch
summary_md: Under oath at the Sanhedrin the King answers the high priest plainly: *And Yahusha (Jesus) said, I am: and you shall see the Son of Adam sitting on the right hand of power, and coming in the clouds of heaven.* (Mark 14:62). He is naming himself by a title the Parables of Enoch had already given to one figure. *And there I saw One who had a head of days, And His head was white like wool, And with Him was another being whose countenance had the appearance of a man, And his face was full of graciousness, like one of the holy angels.* (1 Enoch 46:1). *And he answered and said unto me: This is the Son of Adam who hath righteousness, With whom dwelleth righteousness, And who revealeth all the treasures of that which is hidden, Because Yahuah (Lord) of Spirits hath chosen him, And whose lot hath the pre-eminence before Yahuah (Lord) of Spirits in uprightness for ever.* (1 Enoch 46:3). *And this Son of Adam whom thou hast seen Shall raise up the kings and the mighty from their seats, [And the strong from their thrones] And shall loosen the reins of the strong, And break the teeth of the sinners.* (1 Enoch 46:4). The seating itself comes later in the Parables: *And Yahuah (Lord) of Spirits seated him on the throne of His glory, And the spirit of righteousness was poured out upon him, And the word of his mouth slays all the sinners, And all the unrighteous are destroyed from before his face.* (1 Enoch 62:2). *For from the beginning the Son of Adam was hidden, And the El Elyon (Most High) preserved him in the presence of His might, And revealed him to the elect.* (1 Enoch 62:7). And the rulers who had him bound will do what Enoch said they would: *And all the kings and the mighty and the exalted and those who rule the earth Shall fall down before him on their faces, And worship and set their hope upon that Son of Adam, And petition him and supplicate for mercy at his hands.* (1 Enoch 62:9). The Parables name him beside the Head of Days as a title, the chosen one seated on the throne of glory. Mark's courtroom has that same one standing in the dock, telling the court that condemns him where they will next see him sitting.
note: Degraded prose and Red Line talk removed; 46:1, 3, 4 quoted in full; the old 62:1 and 62:9 quotes were other verses' words (62:2 and 46:4) — replaced with live 62:2, 62:7, 62:9.

title: The worm dieth not and the place of punishment in Judith and 1 Enoch
summary_md: Three times in a row the King says it: *And if your hand offend you, cut it off: it is better for you to enter into life maimed, than having two hands to go into hell, into the fire that never shall be quenched:* (Mark 9:43) *Where their worm dies not, and the fire is not quenched.* (Mark 9:44). The picture is Isaiah's: *And they shall go forth, and look upon the carcases of the men that have transgressed against me: for their worm shall not die, neither shall their fire be quenched; and they shall be an abhorring unto all flesh.* (Isaiah 66:24). Judith sings the same two things together for the day of judgment: *Yahuah (God) Almighty will take vengeance of them in the day of judgment, in putting fire and worms in their flesh; and they shall feel them, and weep for ever.* (Judith 16:17). Enoch was walked through the geography of it. The dead are held first: *And these places have been made to receive them till the day of their judgement and till their appointed period [till the period appointed], till the great judgement (comes) upon them.’* (1 Enoch 22:4). Then he is shown a blessed land full of trees and a cursed valley beside it, and asks what the valley is for: *Then Uriel, one of the holy angels who was with me, answered and said: ‘This accursed valley is for those who are accursed for ever: Here shall all the accursed be gathered together who utter with their lips against Yahuah (Lord) unseemly words and of His glory speak hard things. Here shall they be gathered together, and here shall be their place of judgement.* (1 Enoch 27:2). That cursed valley beside the holy mountain is the valley of Hinnom, and Gehenna, the word Mark uses for hell, is its name. The King is not inventing a place to frighten people with. He is naming the valley Enoch stood over, with Isaiah's worm and Judith's fire, appointed for a day of judgment that has not yet come, after a holding that has an end.
note: Degraded 'framework-honest' prose removed; the old 22:11 quote is the live 22:4, re-quoted; 27:2 quoted in full; Mark, Isaiah from the index, Judith kept as the old summary quoted it.

title: The restoration of the age to come — 1 Enoch 5 and 10, Jubilees 23
summary_md: When John sends from prison to ask whether he is the one, Yahusha (Jesus) answers with what is happening in front of the messengers: *The blind receive their sight, and the lame walk, the lepers are cleansed, and the deaf hear, the dead are raised up, and the poor have the gospel preached to them.* (Matthew 11:5). It is Isaiah's list: *Then the eyes of the blind shall be opened, and the ears of the deaf shall be unstopped.* (Isaiah 35:5). And it is a taste of an age the library had already described in full. Enoch tells what is kept for the elect once the judgment has passed: *And for you the godless there shall be a curse. But for the elect there shall be light and joy and peace, And they shall inherit the earth.* (1 Enoch 5:7). *And then there shall be bestowed upon the elect wisdom, And they shall all live and never again sin, Either through ungodliness or through pride: But they who are wise shall be humble.* (1 Enoch 5:8). *And they shall not again transgress, Nor shall they sin all the days of their life, Nor shall they die of (the divine) anger or wrath, But they shall complete the number of the days of their life. And their lives shall be increased in peace, And the years of their joy shall be multiplied, In eternal gladness and peace, All the days of their life.* (1 Enoch 5:9). The same promise is given to Noah's seed after the Watchers are bound: *And then shall all the righteous escape, And shall live till they beget thousands of children, And all the days of their youth and their old age Shall they complete in peace.* (1 Enoch 10:17). *And then shall the whole earth be tilled in righteousness, and shall all be planted with trees and be full of blessing.* (1 Enoch 10:18). Jubilees 23 says the same of the last days, long life, peace and joy, no Satan and no destroyer, and healing. What John's messengers saw was that age reaching back into theirs, the blind and lame and dead already being handled the way the whole earth will be handled. The day of vengeance in the same breath of Isaiah 61 he left unread, because that part waits for his return.
note: Internal shorthand rewritten; the old 5:7-9 words were not the live text — 5:7, 5:8, 5:9 now quoted in full from the live verses, with 10:17-18; Matthew and Isaiah from the index; Jubilees 23 named in prose (not in the index).

title: Mysteries hidden from the foundation of the world revealed to the elect — 1 Enoch 46 and 48, Wisdom of Solomon 6, 2 Esdras 6
summary_md: *All these things spake Yahusha (Jesus) unto the multitude in parables; and without a parable spake he not unto them:* (Matthew 13:34) *That it might be fulfilled which was spoken by the prophet, saying, I will open my mouth in parables; I will utter things which have been kept secret from the foundation of the world.* (Matthew 13:35). The psalm he is fulfilling is Asaph's, and the pattern of things hidden since the foundation and then opened to a chosen few runs all through the library. Enoch saw the one who does the opening, and was told who he is: *And he answered and said unto me: This is the Son of Adam who hath righteousness, With whom dwelleth righteousness, And who revealeth all the treasures of that which is hidden, Because Yahuah (Lord) of Spirits hath chosen him, And whose lot hath the pre-eminence before Yahuah (Lord) of Spirits in uprightness for ever.* (1 Enoch 46:3). He was himself the first thing hidden: *And for this reason hath he been chosen and hidden before Him, Before the creation of the world and for evermore.* (1 Enoch 48:6). *And the wisdom of Yahuah (Lord) of Spirits hath revealed him to the holy and righteous; For he hath preserved the lot of the righteous, Because they have hated and despised this world of unrighteousness, And have hated all its works and ways in the name of Yahuah (Lord) of Spirits: For in his name they are saved, And according to his good pleasure hath it been in regard to their life.* (1 Enoch 48:7). Solomon speaks the same way as a teacher: *as for wisdom, what she is, and how she came up, I will tell you, and will not hide mysteries from you* (Wisdom of Solomon 6:22), and Ezra is told of the last days when *the truth, which hath been so long without fruit, shall be declared* (2 Esdras 6:28). So when the King speaks in parables to the crowd and opens them to the disciples, he is doing the work Enoch saw the Son of Adam doing, revealing the treasures of what was hidden, and the disciples receive it because, as he had just told them from Isaiah 6, it was given to them to receive. The sower of the good seed in the next verse is this same Son of Adam.
note: Internal shorthand (four moves, Red Line #11, wisdom-stream) rewritten; 46:3, 48:6, 48:7 quoted in full from the live text; Wisdom 6:22 and 2 Esdras 6:28 kept as the old summary quoted them.

title: Names written before the Great One and not blotted out — 1 Enoch 103–104 and confessing or denying him
summary_md: *Whosoever therefore shall confess me before men, him will I confess also before my Father which is in heaven.* (Matthew 10:32). *But whosoever shall deny me before men, him will I also deny before my Father which is in heaven.* (Matthew 10:33). The confessing he promises is a name spoken before the Father, and the library knows the names are already written there. Enoch swears to the righteous what he has read: *That all goodness and joy and glory are prepared for them, And written down for the spirits of those who have died in righteousness, And that manifold good shall be given to you in recompense for your labours, And that your lot is abundantly beyond the lot of the living.* (1 Enoch 103:3). *And the spirits of you who have died in righteousness shall live and rejoice, And their spirits shall not perish, nor their memorial from before the face of the Great One Unto all the generations of the world: wherefore no longer fear their contumely.* (1 Enoch 103:4). And a few lines on: *I swear unto you, that in heaven the angels remember you for good before the glory of the Great One: and your names are written before the glory of the Great One.* (1 Enoch 104:1). Names are written before, and the only thing scripture ever says can happen to a written name is that it is blotted out, at Sinai when Moses pleads, in David's psalm, and in the promise to Sardis: *He that overcomes, the same shall be clothed in white raiment; and I will not blot out his name out of the book of life, but I will confess his name before my Father, and before his angels.* (Revelation 3:5). Confess his name before the Father is the same phrase Matthew 10 uses. The one who lives out the confession keeps a name that was always there; the one who denies him under pressure is risking the blotting, which is why the warning is spoken to those whose names are written and not to anyone else.
note: The old 103:3 and 103:8 quotes were not the live text (the live 103:8 is a woe); re-quoted 103:3-4 and added 104:1, which carries the 'names written' line; Red Line talk removed; Revelation 3:5 from the index; Exodus 32:33 and Psalm 69:28 named in prose.

title: No forgiveness for the hardened heart — Jubilees 15, 1 Enoch 65, Wisdom of Solomon 12
summary_md: *And whosoever speaks a word against the Son of Adam, it shall be forgiven him: but whosoever speaks against the Ruach HaKodesh (Holy Spirit), it shall not be forgiven him, neither in this world, neither in the world to come.* (Matthew 12:32). The men he says this to have just watched the Spirit cast out a demon and called it the work of Beelzebub. They saw the thing clearly and named it the devil's, and that is the hardening the library already knew had no road back from it. Enoch was told it about the ones who had learned the Watchers' secrets and would not turn: *And these—they have no place of repentance for ever, because they have shown them what was hidden, and they are the damned: but as for thee, my son, Yahuah (Lord) of Spirits knows that thou art pure, and guiltless of this reproach concerning the secrets.* (1 Enoch 65:11). Jubilees names the same wrath for the ones who set the covenant aside on purpose: *there will be great wrath from Yahuah (the Lord) ... because they have forsaken His covenant and have turned aside from His word* (Jubilees 15:33-34). And the Wisdom of Solomon says why the patience ran out on the Canaanites: he gave them place for repentance, not being ignorant that their malice was bred in them and that their way of thinking would never change (Wisdom of Solomon 12:10). None of these is about a slip of the tongue. They are about a settled refusal, eyes open, that has made up its mind against the correction. That is why the one who fears he has committed this sin almost certainly has not; the fear is a conscience still working, and a hardened heart does not lie awake over it.
note: Internal shorthand and the four-costume aside rewritten in plain words; 65:11 quoted in full from the live text; Jubilees kept as the old summary quoted it; Wisdom 12:10 (not in index) given in prose; the pastoral reading kept; title plainer.

title: Whose names are in the book of life — the books of the living (Exodus 32, Daniel 12, Malachi 3, 1 Enoch)
summary_md: Paul names his fellowlabourers at Philippi as those *whose names are in the book of life* (Philippians 4:3), and that book is no late invention but the heavenly register the whole library knows. At Sinai Moses appealed to it: *if not, blot me, I pray thee, out of thy book which thou hast written* (Exodus 32:32), and Yahuah (LORD) answered, *Whosoever hath sinned against me, him will I blot out of my book* (Exodus 32:33). Daniel learned that deliverance in the last great trouble belongs to *every one that shall be found written in the book* (Daniel 12:1). Malachi saw it kept for the faithful: *a book of remembrance was written before him for them that feared Yahuah (LORD), and that thought upon his name* (Malachi 3:16), who shall be his *in that day when I make up my jewels* (Malachi 3:17). Enoch watched the very same books opened before the throne: *In those days I saw the Head of Days when He seated himself upon the throne of His glory, And the books of the living were opened before Him: And all His host which is in heaven above and His counsellors stood before Him,* (1 Enoch 47:3). He swore by what he had read in them: *Mighty One in dominion, and by His greatness I swear to you. I know a mystery And have read the heavenly tablets, And have seen the holy books, And have found written therein and inscribed regarding them:* (1 Enoch 103:2). And he knew the dark side of the ledger too: *And wait ye indeed till sin has passed away, for their names shall be blotted out of the book of life and out of the holy books, and their seed shall be destroyed for ever, and their spirits shall be slain, and they shall cry and make lamentation in a place that is a chaotic wilderness, and in the fire shall they burn; for there is no earth there.* (1 Enoch 108:3), the same blotting Yahuah (LORD) spoke of at Sinai. So when Paul says the Philippian partners' names are in the book of life, he is placing them in the one covenant ledger that runs from Moses to Daniel to the throne of the Head of Days, the book of remembrance, the books of the living, in which the righteous are written and kept and not blotted out, gathered as the jewels of Yahuah (LORD).
note: The 104:2 quote ('I have beheld the books of life') is not in Charles; replaced with the live 103:2 ('have seen the holy books'); 47:3 and 108:3 quoted in full from the live text; the rest kept.

title: The plant of righteousness and the Branch
summary_md: When the Watchers are bound and the earth is cleansed, the first thing commanded to grow in it is a plant: *Destroy all wrong from the face of the earth and let every evil work come to an end: and let the plant of righteousness and truth appear: and it shall prove a blessing; the works of righteousness and truth shall be planted in truth and joy for evermore.* (1 Enoch 10:16). The prophets watch for the same growth and call it the Branch. Isaiah's shoot from the stump of Jesse, the *netser*, becomes in the same chapter the ensign the scattered gather to: *And in that day there shall be a root of Jesse, which shall stand for an ensign of the people; to it shall the Gentiles seek: and his rest shall be glorious.* (Isaiah 11:10). Jeremiah names him outright: *Behold, the days come, says Yahuah (LORD), that I will raise unto David a righteous Branch, and a King shall reign and prosper, and shall execute judgment and justice in the earth.* (Jeremiah 23:5). Zechariah calls him *my servant the BRANCH* and says *the man whose name is The BRANCH* shall build the temple of Yahuah (LORD) (Zechariah 3:8; 6:12). Then Matthew brings the child of the promise to live in a town whose name carries the word: *And he came and dwelt in a city called Nazareth: that it might be fulfilled which was spoken by the prophets, He shall be called a Nazarene.* (Matthew 2:23). No single prophet says those words; Matthew says the prophets, and Natsareth is Branch-town. The plant Enoch saw appearing after the judgment, the shoot and the Branch the prophets kept promising, and the boy from Natsareth are one and the same, and the books that carry the first witness to it are the ones the Reformation cut from the library.
note: Degraded 'register / extras-tier' prose rewritten; 10:16 quoted in full (live, same); Isaiah 11:10, Jeremiah 23:5, Matthew 2:23 added from the index; Zechariah named with its two phrases in prose.

title: The sun shall not smite thee by day, nor the moon by night
summary_md: *Yahuah (LORD) is thy keeper: Yahuah (LORD) is thy shade upon thy right hand* (Psalm 121:5), and so *The sun shall not smite thee by day, nor the moon by night* (Psalm 121:6). The same shade shields the returning exiles: *neither shall the heat nor sun smite them: for he that hath mercy on them shall lead them, even by the springs of water shall he guide them* (Isaiah 49:10), and brings them at last where no heat can reach: *neither shall the sun light on them, nor any heat* (Revelation 7:16). The lights themselves are no terror to the one he keeps, because Enoch saw what holds them: *And I saw the chambers of the sun and moon, whence they proceed and whither they come again, and their glorious return, and how one is superior to the other, and their stately orbit, and how they do not leave their orbit, and they add nothing to their orbit and they take nothing from it, and they keep faith with each other, in accordance with the oath by which they are bound together.* (1 Enoch 41:5). *And first the sun goes forth and traverses his path according to the commandment of Yahuah (Lord) of Spirits, and mighty is His name for ever and ever.* (1 Enoch 41:6). Sun and moon are bound by an oath and walk by a commandment. The Keeper who gave the commandment is the one standing at thy right hand, and the lights he rules cannot harm what he shades.
note: The abridged 41:5 quote did not match the live wording; 41:5 and 41:6 now quoted in full; the rest kept.

title: Let Every Thing That Hath Breath Praise Yah — the Consummation of the Psalter
summary_md: The whole Psalter ends on a single, total summons: *Let every thing that hath breath praise Yahuah (LORD). Praise ye Yahuah (LORD)* (Psalm 150:6). Every breathing creature — kol haneshamah — is called, and the breath itself is the clue: it was given at creation, *And Yahuah Elohim (the LORD God) formed man of the dust of the ground, and breathed into his nostrils the breath of life; and man became a living soul* (Genesis 2:7), and it is held by the One *that giveth breath unto the people upon it, and spirit to them that walk therein* (Isaiah 42:5), who *giveth to all life, and breath, and all things* (Acts 17:25). The gift returns as praise. This widens the keystone's closing vow — *let all flesh bless his holy name for ever and ever* (Psalm 145:21) — to the very edge of creation, and it is sworn by Yahuah himself: *unto me every knee shall bow, every tongue shall swear* (Isaiah 45:23), *That at the name of Yahusha (Jesus) every knee should bow, of things in heaven, and things in earth, and things under the earth* (Philippians 2:10). The restored library hears it already sounding above and ahead: *And I heard the voices of those four presences as they uttered praises before Yahuah (Lord) of glory.* (1 Enoch 40:3); and when the Elect One lifts up his countenance to judge, the whole host summoned before him *On that day shall raise one voice, and bless and glorify and exalt in the spirit of faith, and in the spirit of wisdom, and in the spirit of patience, and in the spirit of mercy, and in the spirit of judgement and of peace, and in the spirit of goodness, and shall all say with one voice: "Blessed is He, and may the name of Yahuah (Lord) of Spirits be blessed for ever and ever."* (1 Enoch 61:11); and the *peculiar people above all peoples* are sanctified *to bless Him who has created all things* (Jubilees 2:21). It consummates in John's vision, where *every creature which is in heaven, and on the earth, and under the earth, and such as are in the sea, and all that are in them* cries *Blessing, and honour, and glory, and power, be unto him that sitteth upon the throne, and unto the Lamb for ever and ever* (Revelation 5:13). This is the telos of the whole Psalter: the gathered two-house people and all that breathes, in one final Hallelujah. Praise ye Yah.
note: Mechanical re-quote kept (40:3, 61:11 live); the sentence leading into 61:11 mended so 'On that day shall raise one voice' has its subject.

title: Resurrection from Sheol — the gates of the dead give back what they received — the sign of Yonah in Wisdom of Solomon 16, 1 Enoch 51, Jubilees 23
summary_md: They ask for a sign and he gives them one they cannot see yet: *For as Jonas was three days and three nights in the whale’s belly; so shall the Son of Adam be three days and three nights in the heart of the earth.* (Matthew 12:40). Three days and three nights in the heart of the earth means Sheol, and coming out of it means Sheol gave him back, and the library had been saying for a long time that Sheol will give back. Solomon says it of Yahuah (God): *thou hast power of life and death: thou leadest to the gates of Sheol, and bringest up again* (Wisdom of Solomon 16:13). Enoch says it of the day the Elect One takes the throne: *And in those days shall the earth also give back that which has been entrusted to it, And Sheol also shall give back that which it has received, And hell shall give back that which it owes.* (1 Enoch 51:1). *And he shall choose the righteous and holy from among them: For the day has drawn nigh that they should be saved.* (1 Enoch 51:2). Jubilees promises the servants that *the Lord will heal His servants, And they shall rise up and see great peace* (Jubilees 23:30). The sign of Yonah is the King announcing that he himself will go down through those gates first and be brought up, the firstfruits of what Enoch saw the earth and Sheol do for everyone entrusted to them. The count is a real count. Three days and three nights is what he said, and the Friday evening to Sunday morning the tradition settled on does not hold three nights, which is one more reason to read the week of his death by the calendar of the feasts rather than by the calendar handed down.
note: Internal shorthand rewritten; 51:1-2 quoted in full from the live text; Wisdom and Jubilees kept as the old summary quoted them; Matthew from the index; the literal three-days point kept in plain words.

title: The reed to measure the temple of Elohim (God), and the altar, and them that worship therein (Ezekiel 40)
summary_md: The chapter opens with a measuring: *And there was given me a reed like unto a rod: and the angel stood, saying, Rise, and measure the temple of Elohim (God), and the altar, and them that worship therein.* (Revelation 11:1). This is Ezekiel's reed: *behold, there was a man, whose appearance was like the appearance of brass, with a line of flax in his hand, and a measuring reed* (Ezekiel 40:3), who charged the prophet to *behold with thine eyes... and declare all that thou seest to the house of Yashar'el (Israel)* (Ezekiel 40:4). It is Zechariah's line too, *behold a man with a measuring line in his hand... To measure Jerusalem* (Zechariah 2:1), and that measuring ended in restoration, Yahuah (LORD) himself a wall of fire and the glory in her midst. The measuring is no demolition. It marks off what belongs to Yahuah (LORD), a *separation between the sanctuary and the profane place* (Ezekiel 42:20). The outer court is left out of it: *But the court which is without the temple leave out, and measure it not; for it is given unto the Gentiles: and the holy city shall they tread under foot forty and two months* (Revelation 11:2). Daniel heard the same treading and the same cry, *to give both the sanctuary and the host to be trodden under foot* (Daniel 8:13), and Isaiah grieved it: *our adversaries have trodden down thy sanctuary* (Isaiah 63:18). But the trampling is measured and brief, forty and two months, a little while, and the temple and the worshippers are kept. Enoch saw where the measuring leads. The old house is taken down and carried off, and then: *And I saw till Yahuah (Lord) of the sheep brought a new house greater and loftier than that first, and set it up in the place of the first which had been folded up: all its pillars were new, and its ornaments were new and larger than those of the first, the old one which He had taken away, and all the sheep were within it.* (1 Enoch 90:29). The worshippers counted with the reed are the sheep being gathered into that greater house. To measure the temple is to mark off the regathered Yashar'el (Israel) for the restoration.
note: The 90:17 quote was not Charles's wording; replaced with the live 90:29, which carries the new house with all the sheep in it; the rest kept.

title: Names not written in the book of life of the Lamb slain (Exodus 32, Psalm 69, Daniel 12)
summary_md: *And all that dwell upon the earth shall worship him, whose names are not written in the book of life of the Lamb slain from the foundation of the world.* (Revelation 13:8). The worshippers of the beast are told apart by a book, and it is no new register opened on the day someone believes. It is the book written of old, the one Moses pleaded over at Sinai: *if not, blot me, I pray thee, out of thy book which thou hast written* (Exodus 32:32). It is the *book of the living* the psalmist knew, set over against the company of the saved: *let them be blotted out of the book of the living, and not be written with the righteous* (Psalm 69:28). It is the book that carries Daniel's people through the worst trouble: *And at that time shall Michael stand up, the great prince which stands for the children of your people: and there shall be a time of trouble, such as never was since there was a nation even to that same time: and at that time your people shall be delivered, every one that shall be found written in the book.* (Daniel 12:1). One book runs through all of it, the register of Yahuah (LORD)'s own, the names written from the foundation of the world. Enoch saw it opened at the judgment of the shepherds: *And I saw till a throne was erected in the pleasant land, and Yahuah (Lord) of the sheep sat Himself thereon, and the other took the sealed books and opened those books before Yahuah (Lord) of the sheep.* (1 Enoch 90:20). And earlier, in the Parables, the same books before the same throne: *In those days I saw the Head of Days when He seated himself upon the throne of His glory, And the books of the living were opened before Him: And all His host which is in heaven above and His counsellors stood before Him,* (1 Enoch 47:3). To worship the beast is to be found outside the books of the living. To belong to the Lamb is to have had a name written in his book before the beast ever rose. The Lamb who opens the book is the Lord of the sheep who gathers his own; the writing of the name and the gathering are one act, settled before the foundation of the world, and no confession adds a name that was not there. The patience of the saints rests on that writing. The beast can make war on the body, but it cannot reach the name.
note: The 90:12 quote was invented; replaced with the live 90:20 (sealed books opened before the Lord of the sheep) and 47:3 (books of the living); 'the framework's order' said in plain words; the rest kept, Daniel 12:1 in full from the index.

title: The second beast like a lamb, the false prophet and the fire (Deuteronomy 13, 1 Kings 18, Daniel 3)
summary_md: *And I beheld another beast coming up out of the earth; and he had two horns like a lamb, and he spake as a dragon* (Revelation 13:11). The second beast wears the costume of a lamb and speaks with the dragon's voice. He is the false prophet, and the Torah named his kind long before. *If there arise among you a prophet, or a dreamer of dreams, and giveth thee a sign or a wonder* (Deuteronomy 13:1), and the sign comes to pass, yet he draws you after other gods, *thou shalt not hearken*, for *Yahuah Elohaychem (the LORD your God) proveth you, to know whether ye love Yahuah Elohaychem (the LORD your God) with all your heart* (Deuteronomy 13:3). A sign that comes true is no proof of a true prophet; it is the proving of your loyalty. So when this beast *doeth great wonders, so that he maketh fire come down from heaven on the earth in the sight of men* (Revelation 13:13) and *deceiveth them that dwell on the earth by the means of those miracles* (Revelation 13:14), he is the sign-worker the Torah taught the people to refuse. And the sign he picks is the very one the true Elohim (God) once owned. At Carmel the test was *the Elohim (God) that answereth by fire, let him be Elohim (God)* (1 Kings 18:24), and Yahuah (LORD) alone answered while the false prophets' altar stayed cold. Now the false prophet apes that fire from heaven to claim a proof that was Yahuah (LORD)'s, and it is a deceiver's costume, not the verdict of heaven. His end is an image and an edict: *as many as would not worship the image of the beast should be killed* (Revelation 13:15), the same decree Nebuchadnezzar made, *whoso falleth not down and worshippeth shall the same hour be cast into the midst of a burning fiery furnace* (Daniel 3:6). But the fire he calls down to deceive does not get the last word. Enoch saw the end appointed for the ones who misled the flock: *And the judgement was held first over the stars, and they were judged and found guilty, and went to the place of condemnation, and they were cast into an abyss, full of fire and flaming, and full of pillars of fire.* (1 Enoch 90:24). *And those seventy shepherds were judged and found guilty, and they were cast into that fiery abyss.* (1 Enoch 90:25). The false prophet who calls fire from heaven goes into the fire himself, and the saints who refuse his sign, like the three who would not bow, are kept by the Elohim (God) who is faithful whether he delivers or not.
note: The 90:14 quote was invented; replaced with the live 90:24-25 (the stars and the seventy shepherds cast into the fiery abyss); the rest kept with the dashes eased.

title: The tree of life in the midst of the paradise of Elohim (God) — Eden restored (Genesis 2)
summary_md: The first letter ends with the oldest promise of all: *He that has an ear, let him hear what the Spirit says unto the churches; To him that overcomes will I give to eat of the tree of life, which is in the midst of the paradise of Elohim (God).* (Revelation 2:7). Paradise is Eden by its Greek name, and the tree is the very tree of Genesis: *And out of the ground made Yahuah Elohim (the LORD God) to grow every tree that is pleasant to the sight, and good for food; the tree of life also in the midst of the garden, and the tree of knowledge of good and evil.* (Genesis 2:9). The tree barred to Adam after the fall is set before the overcomer, the old inheritance opened again rather than a new reward. Ezekiel saw it multiplied into a riverside orchard by the waters from the sanctuary: *all trees for meat, whose leaf shall not fade, neither shall the fruit thereof be consumed... and the fruit thereof shall be for meat, and the leaf thereof for medicine* (Ezekiel 47:12). Enoch was shown the same tree, by a mountain that looked like a throne: *And amongst them was a tree such as I had never yet smelt, neither was any amongst them nor were others like it: it had a fragrance beyond all fragrance, and its leaves and blooms and wood wither not for ever: and its fruit is beautiful, and its fruit resembles the dates of a palm.* (1 Enoch 24:4). Michael told him who it is kept for and when: *And as for this fragrant tree no mortal is permitted to touch it till the great judgement, when He shall take vengeance on all and bring (everything) to its consummation for ever. It shall then be given to the righteous and holy.* (1 Enoch 25:4). *Its fruit shall be for food to the elect: it shall be transplanted to the holy place, to the temple of Yahuah (Lord), the Eternal King.* (1 Enoch 25:5). And the book itself shows the promise kept at the end: *In the midst of the street of it, and on either side of the river, was there the tree of life, which bare twelve manner of fruits, and yielded her fruit every month: and the leaves of the tree were for the healing of the nations.* (Revelation 22:2). Genesis bars the tree; Ezekiel and Enoch see it reserved; the letter promises it; the new Jerusalem throws it open. It is one unbroken hope, Eden brought to its end, the curse undone, the tree given freely to the one who keeps the works unto the end.
note: The old 24:11 does not exist live (its words are 25:5); 24:4 and 25:4-5 quoted in full; Revelation 2:7, 22:2 and Genesis 2:9 in full from the index; the draft's broken 'whose fruit Its fruit' sentence mended.

title: The books were opened, and the book of life (Daniel 7 and 12, Malachi 3)
summary_md: *And I saw the dead, small and great, stand before Elohim (God); and the books were opened: and another book was opened, which is the book of life: and the dead were judged out of those things which were written in the books, according to their works.* (Revelation 20:12). Daniel saw the like: *A fiery stream issued and came forth from before him: thousand thousands ministered unto him, and ten thousand times ten thousand stood before him: the judgment was set, and the books were opened.* (Daniel 7:10). This is the one reckoning of the dead the seventh trumpet already sounded, *the time of the dead, that they should be judged* (Revelation 11:18), shown here again in full. Daniel was told deliverance comes to *every one that shall be found written in the book* (Daniel 12:1), and that *many of them that sleep in the dust of the earth shall awake, some to everlasting life, and some to shame and everlasting contempt* (Daniel 12:2), the very division that falls at the throne, some found written in the book of life and some cast into the lake of fire. The book of the living the psalmist knew can be blotted out, *Let them be blotted out of the book of the living, and not be written with the righteous* (Psalm 69:28); names are written and never added, but they can be blotted. Malachi names the same record kept for the faithful: *a book of remembrance was written before him for them that feared Yahuah (LORD), and that thought upon his name* (Malachi 3:16). And the works are recorded and repaid, as Isaiah heard: *Behold, it is written before me: I will not keep silence, but will recompense* (Isaiah 65:6). Enoch saw the scene itself, twice. *In those days I saw the Head of Days when He seated himself upon the throne of His glory, And the books of the living were opened before Him: And all His host which is in heaven above and His counsellors stood before Him,* (1 Enoch 47:3). *And I saw till a throne was erected in the pleasant land, and Yahuah (Lord) of the sheep sat Himself thereon, and the other took the sealed books and opened those books before Yahuah (Lord) of the sheep.* (1 Enoch 90:20). And the book of life is named already in the Apocalypse: *the book of life of the Lamb slain from the foundation of the world* (Revelation 13:8), the names written before the world was. The books of works and the book of life are opened together, and *And whosoever was not found written in the book of life was cast into the lake of fire.* (Revelation 20:15).
note: The 90:12 quote was invented; replaced with the live 90:20; 47:3, Revelation 20:12, 20:15 and Daniel 7:10 quoted in full from the index; the rest kept.

title: The tree of life, and the leaves for the healing of the nations — Eden restored (Genesis 2, Ezekiel 47, 1 Enoch 24–25, 2 Esdras 8)
summary_md: The story closes where it opened, in a garden, but the garden has become a city, and the tree once guarded stands open in the street: *In the midst of the street of it, and on either side of the river, was there the tree of life, which bare twelve manner of fruits, and yielded her fruit every month: and the leaves of the tree were for the healing of the nations.* (Revelation 22:2). This is the very tree of Eden, *the tree of life also in the midst of the garden* (Genesis 2:9). It stood in the midst of the garden at the first; it stands in the midst of the street at the last. After the fall the way to it was shut: *lest he put forth his hand, and take also of the tree of life, and eat, and live for ever* (Genesis 3:22), and *Cherubims, and a flaming sword which turned every way* were set *to keep the way of the tree of life* (Genesis 3:24). Now the guard is withdrawn and the tree is given back to the obedient (Revelation 22:14). It is Ezekiel's river-tree fulfilled, the trees by the temple-waters that bore *new fruit according to his months,* whose *fruit thereof shall be for meat, and the leaf thereof for medicine* (Ezekiel 47:12); the monthly fruit and the healing leaf are John's twelve manner of fruits and leaves for the healing of the nations. Enoch saw this tree and could not stop looking at it: *And amongst them was a tree such as I had never yet smelt, neither was any amongst them nor were others like it: it had a fragrance beyond all fragrance, and its leaves and blooms and wood wither not for ever: and its fruit is beautiful, and its fruit resembles the dates of a palm.* (1 Enoch 24:4). He was told when it would be eaten and where it would stand: *And as for this fragrant tree no mortal is permitted to touch it till the great judgement, when He shall take vengeance on all and bring (everything) to its consummation for ever. It shall then be given to the righteous and holy.* (1 Enoch 25:4). *Its fruit shall be for food to the elect: it shall be transplanted to the holy place, to the temple of Yahuah (Lord), the Eternal King.* (1 Enoch 25:5). John is looking at the transplanting done, the tree kept till the great judgment now standing in the holy city for the righteous to eat. And 2 Esdras names the whole vision in one breath: *to you is paradise opened, the tree of life is planted... a city is builded* (2 Esdras 8:52), one hope and not three, Eden become the new Jerusalem. So the promise sworn at the book's opening is kept at its close: *To him that overcometh will I give to eat of the tree of life, which is in the midst of the paradise of Elohim (God)* (Revelation 2:7). The paradise of Elohim (God) is Eden restored; the overcomer eats of the tree at last, and its leaves heal the nations.

title: Sardis: a name that thou livest and art dead — the book of life, names not blotted out (Exodus 32, Daniel 12)
summary_md: To Sardis, the assembly with *a name that thou livest, and art dead* (Revelation 3:1), the slain and living one speaks of the book that decides the living from the dead. The overcomer *shall be clothed in white raiment; and I will not blot out his name out of the book of life, but I will confess his name before my Father, and before his angels* (Revelation 3:5). The book is not new. It is the book Moses pleaded over at the foot of Sinai, *blot me, I pray thee, out of thy book which thou hast written* (Exodus 32:32), and the book whose blotting answers sin, *Whosoever hath sinned against me, him will I blot out of my book* (Exodus 32:33). It is the book Daniel saw run the deliverance: *at that time thy people shall be delivered, every one that shall be found written in the book* (Daniel 12:1). It is the book the psalmist named against the persecutors: *Let them be blotted out of the book of the living, and not be written with the righteous* (Psalm 69:28). Enoch keeps the same picture whole. To the righteous: *I swear unto you, that in heaven the angels remember you for good before the glory of the Great One: and your names are written before the glory of the Great One.* (1 Enoch 104:1). Of the sinners: *And wait ye indeed till sin has passed away, for their names shall be blotted out of the book of life and out of the holy books, and their seed shall be destroyed for ever, and their spirits shall be slain, and they shall cry and make lamentation in a place that is a chaotic wilderness, and in the fire shall they burn; for there is no earth there.* (1 Enoch 108:3). So the warning to Sardis sits inside a promise. The name written can be struck, and therefore *be watchful, and strengthen the things which remain, that are ready to die* (Revelation 3:2); keep the place in the book that defiling the garments would forfeit. And the promise closes with the confessing the Messiah spoke of in the gospel: *Whosoever therefore shall confess me before men, him will I confess also before my Father which is in heaven.* (Matthew 10:32); *Also I say unto you, Whosoever shall confess me before men, him shall the Son of Adam also confess before the angels of Elohim (God):* (Luke 12:8). The overcomer who held the name on earth is owned by name before the Father and his angels, the Formed Son confessing his own before the Formless.

title: The elders cast their crowns, and the myriads before the throne (1 Enoch 40, Nehemiah 9)
summary_md: Round about the throne sit *four and twenty elders... clothed in white raiment; and they had on their heads crowns of gold* (Revelation 4:4); and when the living creatures give glory, *The four and twenty elders fall down before him that sat on the throne, and worship him that lives for ever and ever, and cast their crowns before the throne, saying,* (Revelation 4:10). They lay their own crowns down before the only One who is worthy. Enoch stood in front of the same worship and could not count it: *And after that I saw thousands of thousands and ten thousand times ten thousand, I saw a multitude beyond number and reckoning, who stood before Yahuah (Lord) of Spirits.* (1 Enoch 40:1). He had seen the throne they stand before as well: *The flaming fire was round about Him, and a great fire stood before Him, and none around could draw nigh Him: ten thousand times ten thousand (stood) before Him, yet He needed no counsellor.* (1 Enoch 14:22). The enthroned elders are part of that host. And Nehemiah's Levites confessed the ground of it all: *thou, even thou, art Yahuah (LORD) alone; thou hast made heaven, the heaven of heavens, with all their host... and the host of heaven worshippeth thee* (Nehemiah 9:6). The host that worships the Maker in the Levites' prayer is the host that gives *glory and honour and thanks to him that sat on the throne* (Revelation 4:9) in John's vision. The elders cast down their crowns because the throne is the Creator's throne, and every crown of gold goes back to the One who made the heads that wear them.

title: Ten thousand times ten thousand — the myriads before the throne (Daniel 7, 1 Enoch)
summary_md: Around the throne John hears a host beyond counting take up the praise of the Lamb: *And I beheld, and I heard the voice of many angels round about the throne and the beasts and the elders: and the number of them was ten thousand times ten thousand, and thousands of thousands;* (Revelation 5:11). The count is Daniel's, word for word: *A fiery stream issued and came forth from before him: thousand thousands ministered unto him, and ten thousand times ten thousand stood before him: the judgment was set, and the books were opened.* (Daniel 7:10). Daniel saw that court before the Ancient of days; John sees it round about the throne, lifting its voice to the Lamb who has just taken the book. Enoch counted the same way when he was carried up: *The flaming fire was round about Him, and a great fire stood before Him, and none around could draw nigh Him: ten thousand times ten thousand (stood) before Him, yet He needed no counsellor.* (1 Enoch 14:22). *And after that I saw thousands of thousands and ten thousand times ten thousand, I saw a multitude beyond number and reckoning, who stood before Yahuah (Lord) of Spirits.* (1 Enoch 40:1). And he heard what the host's voices were for: *The first voice blesses Yahuah (Lord) of Spirits for ever and ever.* (1 Enoch 40:4). *And the second voice I heard blessing the Elect One and the elect ones who hang upon Yahuah (Lord) of Spirits.* (1 Enoch 40:5). The One on the throne blessed, and the Elect One beside him blessed, is exactly the shape of Revelation 5, where the One who sits and the Lamb are praised together. The host's cry is the sevenfold one: *Saying with a loud voice, Worthy is the Lamb that was slain to receive power, and riches, and wisdom, and strength, and honour, and glory, and blessing.* (Revelation 5:12). The court that could not be counted before the Father now lifts its voice to the slain Lamb.

title: The rich man and Lazaros — Sheol with its divisions, and *they have Mosheh and the prophets*
summary_md: Lazaros, full of sores and laid at the gate with the dogs licking him, dies and *was carried by the angels into Abraham’s bosom: the rich man also died, and was buried;* (Luke 16:22). *And in hell he lift up his eyes, being in torments, and sees Abraham afar off, and Lazarus in his bosom.* (Luke 16:23). The dead in this parable remember, the rich man knows he has five brothers; they see, across a gulf; they are still themselves, Lazaros still Lazaros and the rich man still the rich man. And the two places are divided: *And beside all this, between us and you there is a great gulf fixed: so that they which would pass from hence to you cannot; neither can they pass to us, that would come from thence.* (Luke 16:26). Two inherited teachings both stumble here. The one that says the dead sleep without knowing anything has to explain away a conversation. The one that says the torment is the final and eternal state has to ignore that this is Sheol before the resurrection, a holding place and not a verdict. Enoch was shown the holding place and told how it is arranged: *And he answered me and said unto me: ‘These three have been made that the spirits of the dead might be separated. And such a division has been made for the spirits of the righteous, in which there is the bright spring of water.* (1 Enoch 22:9). *And such has been made for sinners when they die and are buried in the earth and judgement has not been executed on them in their lifetime.* (1 Enoch 22:10). *Here their spirits shall be set apart in this great pain till the great day of judgement and punishment and torment of those who curse for ever and retribution for their spirits. There He shall bind them for ever.* (1 Enoch 22:11). Awake, divided, and waiting for the great day: that is what the rich man is doing, and the parable only makes sense if that is where he is. Then the parable turns to the living. The rich man wants a messenger sent to his brothers, and Abraham answers, *they have Mosheh (Moses) and the prophets; let them hear them. If they hear not Mosheh (Moses) and the prophets, neither will they be persuaded, though one rose from the dead* (Luke 16:29, 31). That is the King's standing test against every gospel that sets the Torah aside, and it was proved in the open when another Lazaros was raised at John 11 and the chief priests set about killing him. Five brothers, the leadership of the house of Yahudah (Judah), who would not hear Moses, and so did not believe when one rose.

title: The righteous shall shine as the sun in the kingdom of their Father — 1 Enoch 104, 2 Esdras 7, Wisdom of Solomon 3
summary_md: When the King explains the tares he ends with what the wheat will look like once the field is cleared: *Then shall the righteous shine forth as the sun in the kingdom of their Father. Who has ears to hear, let him hear.* (Matthew 13:43). Daniel heard it first: *And they that be wise shall shine as the brightness of the firmament; and they that turn many to righteousness as the stars for ever and ever.* (Daniel 12:3). And the rest of the library says it in the same words. Enoch, to the righteous who have been shamed: *Be hopeful; for aforetime ye were put to shame through ill and affliction; but now ye shall shine as the lights of heaven, ye shall shine and ye shall be seen, and the portals of heaven shall be opened to you.* (1 Enoch 104:2). Ezra is shown the orders of the righteous after death, and *the sixth order, when it is shewed them how their face shall shine as the sun, and how they shall be made like unto the light of the stars, being henceforth incorruptible* (2 Esdras 7:97), and later that *the faces of them which have used abstinence shall shine above the stars* (2 Esdras 7:125). Solomon sets the shining on the day of visitation, in harvest language: *in the time of their visitation they shall shine, and run to and fro like sparks among the stubble* (Wisdom of Solomon 3:7). Sparks among the stubble is the same picture as the parable, the righteous bright against the burning tares on the day the two are separated. The shining belongs to the wheat that was gathered and came through the sifting with fruit on it, and the King says so by putting the sentence where he puts it, right after the tares are bound and burned.

title: The seed war from Genesis 3 forward, with the devil as the source of death — Wisdom of Solomon 2:24, 1 Enoch 22, Jubilees 4
summary_md: *The field is the world; the good seed are the children of the kingdom; but the tares are the children of the wicked one;* (Matthew 13:38). *The enemy that sowed them is the devil; the harvest is the end of the world; and the reapers are the angels.* (Matthew 13:39). Two seeds in one field, and the devil the one who sowed the second. The library had been saying this since the garden. Solomon names the devil as the source of death itself: *through envy of the devil came death into the world: and they that do hold of his side do find it* (Wisdom of Solomon 2:24). The first fruit of that seed was Cain, and Enoch was shown his brother's spirit still crying out: *I saw the spirits of the children of men who were dead, and their voice went forth to heaven and made suit.* (1 Enoch 22:5). *Then I asked Raphael the angel who was with me, and I said unto him: ‘This spirit—whose is it, whose voice goeth forth and maketh suit?’* (1 Enoch 22:6). *And he answered me saying: ‘This is the spirit which went forth from Abel, whom his brother Cain slew, and he makes his suit against him till his seed is destroyed from the face of the earth, and his seed is annihilated from amongst the seed of men.’* (1 Enoch 22:7). Abel's suit is against a seed, not only a man. Jubilees tells the murder the way Genesis does, *Qayin (Cain) slew Hevel (Abel) because (God) accepted the sacrifice of Hevel (Abel), and did not accept the offering of Qayin (Cain) ... and his blood cried from the ground to heaven* (Jubilees 4:2), and John names which seed Cain was: *Not as Cain, who was of that wicked one, and slew his brother. And wherefore slew he him? Because his own works were evil, and his brother’s righteous.* (1 John 3:12). So the parable is not a new idea about the world. The serpent in the garden, the envy that brought death in, the Watchers' corruption, the tares in the field, and the harvest where the angels sort them are one story, and Abel's voice has been making suit through all of it until the seed that killed him is gone from among the seed of men.

title: The Son of Adam named before creation
summary_md: The Parables of Enoch name the Son of Adam before anything was made. *And at that hour that Son of Adam was named In the presence of Yahuah (Lord) of Spirits, And his name before the Head of Days.* (1 Enoch 48:2). *Yea, before the sun and the signs were created, Before the stars of the heaven were made, His name was named before Yahuah (Lord) of Spirits.* (1 Enoch 48:3). *And for this reason hath he been chosen and hidden before Him, Before the creation of the world and for evermore.* (1 Enoch 48:6). The one who was named first is then seated: *And Yahuah (Lord) of Spirits seated him on the throne of His glory, And the spirit of righteousness was poured out upon him, And the word of his mouth slays all the sinners, And all the unrighteous are destroyed from before his face.* (1 Enoch 62:2). And at the close of the third Parable his name is made known to the holy ones and they rejoice: *And there was great joy amongst them, And they blessed and glorified and extolled Because the name of that Son of Adam had been revealed unto them.* (1 Enoch 69:26). John says the same of the Word: *In the beginning was the Word, and the Word was with Elohim (God), and the Word was Elohim (God).* (John 1:1). Micah says it of the ruler out of Bethlehem, *whose goings forth have been from of old, from everlasting* (Micah 5:2). The one with a name before the stars, who was with the Father and went forth from him, is the one who appeared and spoke and walked with the fathers all through the Torah and the prophets. And then the name that was hidden is spoken to Joseph by an angel: *And she shall bring forth a son, and you shall call his name Yahusha (JESUS): for he shall save his people from their sins.* (Matthew 1:21), and set beside it, Immanuel, Elohim (God) with us (Matthew 1:23). Enoch knew the name was there before the gospel ever announced it.

title: The Spirit-anointed Elect One — the spirit of wisdom and the spirit of righteousness poured out on the Son in 1 Enoch 49 and 62
summary_md: Matthew explains the King's quiet ministry by quoting Isaiah: *Behold my servant, whom I have chosen; my beloved, in whom my soul is well pleased: I will put my spirit upon him, and he shall shew judgment to the Gentiles.* (Matthew 12:18). The prophet's own words are these: *Behold my servant, whom I uphold; my elect, in whom my soul delights; I have put my spirit upon him: he shall bring forth judgment to the Gentiles.* (Isaiah 42:1). Isaiah had already said what that Spirit would be: *And the spirit of Yahuah (LORD) shall rest upon him, the spirit of wisdom and understanding, the spirit of counsel and might, the spirit of knowledge and of the fear of Yahuah (LORD);* (Isaiah 11:2). Enoch saw the same Spirit on the same chosen one and calls him by Isaiah's word, the Elect One. *For wisdom is poured out like water, And glory faileth not before him for evermore.* (1 Enoch 49:1). *And in him dwells the spirit of wisdom, And the spirit which gives insight, And the spirit of understanding and of might, And the spirit of those who have fallen asleep in righteousness.* (1 Enoch 49:3). And when he is seated to judge: *And Yahuah (Lord) of Spirits seated him on the throne of His glory, And the spirit of righteousness was poured out upon him, And the word of his mouth slays all the sinners, And all the unrighteous are destroyed from before his face.* (1 Enoch 62:2). Isaiah's servant, Enoch's Elect One, and the man the Spirit came down on at the Jordan are one. In this age the anointing shows itself in the way Matthew goes on to describe, a bruised reed he will not break and no voice raised in the streets. At the throne of glory it shows itself as the word of his mouth bringing judgment to victory, which is where Matthew's quotation ends and where Enoch's Parable sits.

title: The Spirit of Wisdom on the Elect One
summary_md: *And Yahusha (Jesus), when he was baptized, went up straightway out of the water: and, lo, the heavens were opened unto him, and he saw the Spirit of Elohim (God) descending like a dove, and lighting upon him:* (Matthew 3:16). The Spirit that came down at the Jordan was not new to the library. Solomon had described her at length, *holy, one only, manifold, subtil, lively, clear, undefiled* and more, and said where she comes from: *the breath of the power of Yahuah (God), and a pure influence flowing from the glory of the Almighty* (Wisdom of Solomon 7:25). The dove coming down is that breath made visible, going out from the Father and resting on the Son. Enoch saw the resting itself: *And in him dwells the spirit of wisdom, And the spirit which gives insight, And the spirit of understanding and of might, And the spirit of those who have fallen asleep in righteousness.* (1 Enoch 49:3). It is Isaiah's list for the Branch: *And the spirit of Yahuah (LORD) shall rest upon him, the spirit of wisdom and understanding, the spirit of counsel and might, the spirit of knowledge and of the fear of Yahuah (LORD);* (Isaiah 11:2). The Spirit in these books is Yahuah's own breath, flowing from his glory and resting on the one he chose, and that is the Spirit the gospel inherits at the immersion, before anyone had built a grid of three equal persons to put her in.
